input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language elsewhere in the Agreement. It restricts Client's assignment rights with only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out: there is no carve-out for a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, the consent standard is unqualified (TrueLink could withhold approval arbitrarily), and nothing prevents TrueLink from assigning the hosting/licensing relationship to a Client competitor. This falls short of the preferred position, though it is not walk-away territory since the prohibition is mutual and TrueLink has no express change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirms a Client change of control is neither an assignment nor a TrueLink termination trigger.

proposal.summary: Add Client affiliate/successor (M&A) assignment carve-out, reasonable consent standard, no assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirm a Client change of control is not an assignment or termination trigger.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a carve-out so we may assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, made the consent standard "not unreasonably withheld," barred assignment by TrueLink to our competitors, and confirmed that a change of control of Client is not an assignment or a termination/re-pricing trigger. This reflects our standard position that corporate reorganizations must not require vendor consent; if helpful, we can accept a mutual successor carve-out with written notice instead.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided, that no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any competitor of Client. No change of control of Client shall be deemed an assignment or transfer, or give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
